about: Where each engine's upstream releases are read and how a release is installed beside the builds already here (collectors/engine_builds.py reads it; workflow/engine_update.py installs). This moves a machine's current build only, never the pin (data/engine_pins.json; docs/engine-upgrade-audit.md). Releases only: rc, dev, alpha, beta, local builds and GitHub prereleases never count. source: github (the latest release; tag picks and reads the version), pypi (the JSON API's releases with a file not yanked), simple (a PEP 503 index page, dist's wheel and sdist names). requires: what a release declares it needs, read from its published metadata before anything installs (unreadable: not installed). paths: the env var each build answers for, relative to its folder; a list is tried in order. version: how a build says its version and commit (argv on the env var's path, patterns; group 1 of the first that matches).

llama.cpp.why: llama.cpp's v0.x release line; the bNNNNN builds are published several times a day and marked prerelease: nightlies (owner, 2026-11-08)

install.why_clone: the full commit history without trees: llama.cpp's cmake counts commits for the build number a run records (a one-commit clone counted 1)

install.check: import vllm, torch; print('vllm', vllm.__version__, 'torch', torch.__version__)

requires.why: requires_python and the torch and cuda-python constraints from the release's metadata; the wheels for this Python and machine from NVIDIA's index; the least driver for that CUDA major (NVIDIA's minor-version compatibility)

install.why: torch first at the release's own constraint from the CUDA index, then the release with that torch pinned; pyarrow < 20 because tensorrt_llm pins numpy < 2 (tools/pod-setup.sh step 4)
install.check: import tensorrt_llm, torch; print('tensorrt_llm', tensorrt_llm.__version__, 'torch', torch.__version__)
